submissions.market_view: S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at records as oil and Treasury yields eased, led by AI infrastructure (MRVL investor day) and nuclear power (CEG-Google, VST DOE loan), while small caps and healthcare lagged. Breadth is narrow and the 10-year sits near 5.3%, so I favor names with confirmed fresh catalysts and keep stops tight.
lessons: First scored night: no closed trades yet, so tonight's lesson is about process, not results. Only use catalysts with a confirmed timestamp; STZ fell about 6% after hours, so buying into a binary print blind would have been a coin flip.

Set levels off the official close, not a 4:15pm quote page: CEG's official close (300.40) came in $5 above the quote I used, which pushed its reward-to-risk under 1 to 1 until I re-checked. Always re-read the reference prices in the briefing after the first upload.
Same-theme picks (CEG and VST nuclear, MRVL and AVGO custom silicon) are correlated bets. Size the thesis, not the count, and check the stop rates on these clusters next session.

picks.thesis: Fiscal Q4 crushed estimates (non-GAAP EPS $1.00 vs ~$0.75; sales $567M, +68% y/y vs ~$519M), and FY27 guidance calls for ~40% sales growth and $4.45 non-GAAP EPS with six new AI-infrastructure customers. Shares were up ~7% after hours, and analyst target hikes should land before the open.
picks.main_risk: The after-hours gap fades as holders take profits after a 188% YTD run, or the call raises questions about gross margin or the $750M convert.

picks.thesis: Q1 FY27 beat (adj. EPS $0.08 vs $0.05, 8.1% core growth, adj. EBITDA margin up to 18.7%) and FY revenue/EBITDA guidance was raised after a 7% drop today. The investor day at 9am ET Wednesday adds a second catalyst, and the stock was up ~10% after hours.
picks.main_risk: Investor day long-term targets disappoint or the Petrifilm transition gets flagged as a risk, so the after-hours pop reverses.

picks.thesis: Investor day set FY28 revenue at ~$20B and FY31 at $70-90B with $30+ EPS. Evercore lifted its target to $433 from $275, and more sell-side target raises should come out overnight and pull in buyers chasing the $300 breakout.
picks.main_risk: RSI above 70 after a 239% YTD gain, so day-two 'sell the news' profit-taking could hit if analyst raises are already priced in.

picks.thesis: A $4.2B DOE loan for nuclear uprates tied to Meta's AI load, plus the read-through from Constellation's Google deal, lifted VST ~11% on 14M+ shares and back above its 200-day. I expect analyst target hikes and follow-through buying toward the $170s.
picks.main_risk: A one-day sector squeeze that mean-reverts, especially if yields rise again.

picks.thesis: Google signed a 20-year, 3,590 MW deal (890 MW of new uprate capacity, $4.3B of investment), the second hyperscaler contract in a week after Amazon. The stock still sits about 28% below its 52-week high, so I expect target raises and continued re-rating on Wednesday.
picks.main_risk: The +12% day already priced most of it, and the deal's pricing terms weren't disclosed.

picks.thesis: Beat and raise: adj. EPS $0.75 vs $0.59, FY27 EPS guidance raised to $3.05-3.35, North America EBITDA +11%. The stock faded from a $50.19 intraday high to close at $47.91, so there's room for post-earnings drift as estimates move up.
picks.catalyst_time: 2026-10-06 pre-market earnings; estimate revisions this week
picks.main_risk: The international segment (EBITDA -54%) and staples-sector weakness cap the move.

picks.thesis: Reports FQ1 after the close on Oct 7 (consensus revenue ~$125M, +94% y/y) with four straight double beats, about 21% short interest and the stock roughly 50% off its high. I'm holding through the print to catch a squeeze on new lease or Finland 1GW updates.
picks.main_risk: A binary earnings gap down on wider losses, capex or financing (dilution) worries.

picks.thesis: Marvell's investor day made the case that hyperscalers prefer custom ASICs. AVGO, the custom-silicon leader, rose ~4% in sympathy but still trades about 24% below its $495 high, with a consensus target around $503, leaving room for a multi-day re-rating.
picks.catalyst_time: 2026-10-06 MRVL investor day read-through; this week
picks.main_risk: Megacap AI rotation stalls if yields push back above 5.3%.

picks.thesis: Reports Q3 before the open Friday Oct 9 (EPS est ~$1.94). Crude is falling on G7 reserve releases, and Delta has guided that fare strength holds, so I'm positioning for a run-up and a beat with the stock 13% under its 52-week high.
picks.main_risk: Q4 guide flags fuel or demand softness; oil rebounds on Middle East supply news.

picks.thesis: Q3 earnings Oct 13 before the open falls inside a 5-session hold. Last quarter equities trading jumped 86%, and record-level markets plus heavy M&A this week (PTC $22.6B, OPCH $5.8B, RXO $5.8B) point to strong IB and markets fees, so I'm positioning for a pre-print run-up.
picks.main_risk: Credit or NII guide disappoints with yields near 24-year highs; banks lag in a tech-led tape.

picks.thesis: The core AI compute franchise, near a $6T market cap, at about 30x trailing P/E with a consensus target around $343. AMD's comment that compute demand is outrunning supply supports another strong print on Nov 25.
picks.main_risk: AI capex digestion or concentration unwind; export restrictions.

picks.thesis: About 17x earnings for search, YouTube, Cloud and TPU custom silicon, and it's locking in long-term clean power (Constellation deal) to scale AI. It trades ~15% under its 52-week high with a consensus target around $426.
picks.main_risk: Antitrust remedies or AI search disruption to ad revenue.

picks.thesis: Azure plus Copilot monetization and an enterprise moat, at about 29x P/E, just under its $553 high, with a consensus target around $568. Steady compounding into late-October earnings.
picks.main_risk: Capex intensity weighs on margins; OpenAI relationship changes.

picks.thesis: AWS AI demand plus retail margin expansion and advertising, at about 20x P/E and 11% below its $287 high, with a consensus target around $330. It has rare valuation support among AI megacaps.
picks.main_risk: AWS share loss to Azure or Google Cloud; consumer slowdown with 5%+ yields.

picks.thesis: The GLP-1 franchise leader (Zepbound/Mounjaro plus oral Foundayo, which showed a significant cardiovascular-risk reduction in Phase 3) with an expanding oncology label (Jaypirca first-line CLL approval). It held up while healthcare sold off and trades ~10% under its 52-week high.
picks.catalyst_time: Ongoing; Q3 earnings late October/early November
picks.main_risk: GLP-1 pricing pressure or Medicare negotiation headlines; sector-wide healthcare de-rating.
